packages.label: מַחֲשָׁבוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת וְחַיּוֹת טְהוֹרוֹת
packages.reason: Holy thoughts and pure animals are two expressions of the same positive spiritual quality — the living volitional force (chayot) of the soul when it is oriented toward holiness. The Rebbe uses the metaphor of pure animals fighting in the arena to illuminate the nature of holy thoughts: both are the same spiritual force (chayot = living force) expressed in two registers — the metaphorical-physical (pure animals) and the mental-spiritual (holy thoughts). They are not cause and effect; they are the same essential reality seen from two angles.

packages.label: מַחֲשָׁבוֹת רָעוֹת וְחַיּוֹת טְמֵאוֹת
packages.reason: Evil thoughts and impure animals are two expressions of the same negative spiritual quality — the living force of the soul when it is captured by impurity and opposition to holiness. The impure animals (chayot teme'ot) are the structural archetype; evil thoughts are the manifestation of the same impure living-force within the human mind. They share the same essential nature: they are both expressions of the unclean animating drive that opposes the sacred. This is the perfect evil mirror of Package 1: where Package 1 is the holy chayot-force expressed as holy thoughts, Package 2 is the same chayot-force expressed as evil thoughts — same structure, opposite orientation.
